title: Bihar Man Arrested After Wife's Killing in Munger, Police Say He Surrendered
excerpt: Police in Jamalpur say the 55-year-old retired loco pilot surrendered with the couple's two daughters after his 28-year-old wife was found dead at their rented home. The motive remains under investigation.
body:
• Police in Jamalpur, in Bihar's Munger district, say Dashrath Mandal, 55, was arrested after he surrendered at the police station following the killing of his wife, Pooja Devi, 28, on Wednesday night.
  • Police say the couple's two daughters, aged eight and five, were in the home; reports say the accused told the children they would get a new mother, an allegation attributed to the children and family accounts in reporting.
  • The body was sent for post-mortem examination and a weapon was recovered, police said; the motive is still under investigation.
  • The victim's family has alleged years of harassment; police say further legal action will follow registration of an FIR based on the family's complaint.

Police in Bihar's Munger district have arrested a 55-year-old retired railway loco pilot after his wife was found dead at their rented home in Jamalpur town, and police say the man surrendered at the local police station with the couple's two young daughters.

The victim was identified in reporting as Pooja Devi, 28. She had married Dashrath Mandal in 2015 and was originally from Ishakchak in Bhagalpur, according to the accounts. Mandal is a resident of the Dharhara police station area and had taken voluntary retirement from the railways, where he worked as a locomotive pilot. The couple lived in a rented house near Sadar Bazaar in Jamalpur, under Adarsh Jamalpur police station limits, with their daughters, aged eight and five.

What police and reports say happened

The killing took place on Wednesday night, November 11, at the family's home. According to preliminary accounts reported from police information, the accused allegedly locked the two children in a separate room before attacking his wife with a sharp weapon. Her body was later found in a locked room at the residence. Police recovered a weapon believed to have been used in the attack from the spot and sent the body for post-mortem examination; Daily Kiran reported the body was sent to Sadar Hospital for autopsy.

Reports say that after the incident the accused locked the room containing the body, covered it, and took the two girls to the police station, where he surrendered. One reported detail, carried in the Times of India account summarised in other reporting, is that he allegedly told the daughters, "Your mother is dead, we'll get you a new mother." That wording is an allegation from that account, not a statement police have independently published, and The Videshi reports it only as attributed.

Jamalpur police informed the victim's brother late on Wednesday night, around 12:30 a.m., according to family accounts in Daily Kiran. Family members who arrived at the scene found her deceased. Police and forensic teams attended the location to investigate.

Police action and investigation

Jamalpur Station House Officer Pankaj Kumar — named as Pankaj Kumar Paswan in one report — said police are investigating the motive and circumstances of the crime. Police said the accused has been arrested and that further legal action will be taken after the necessary procedures and registration of an FIR based on the family's complaint.

On motive, police have not announced a conclusion. One line reported from preliminary investigation is that police suspect the accused's suspicion about his wife's relationships may have been a factor, while investigators said all possible angles were being examined. That suspicion is a police line of inquiry as reported, not an established finding, and no evidence for it has been published.

Family allegations

The victim's family has made separate allegations about the marriage. Her brother Shubham said the family spoke to her two days earlier and that she had not mentioned a serious problem at that time. He alleged that the accused and some relatives had harassed and assaulted her for nearly five years and had frequently questioned her character. Daily Kiran similarly reported relatives claiming she had faced physical and mental abuse for an extended period, and that about a year ago a violent incident led to a police complaint that was later settled.

Those family allegations are part of the complaint and investigation record as reported; they have not been tested in court. Police say the investigation into motive and circumstances is ongoing, and The Videshi will update this story if police publish an FIR, a post-mortem finding, or a charge sheet.
